summary: Ruth Fuller Sasaki (1892–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University (2014) under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later serving as an ANU research associate and Munich postdoctoral researcher (attested 2016).

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She earned her PhD at Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988), and became James P. Storer Associate Professor at Kenyon College.

Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2017) under the doctoral supervision of Jason Neelis.

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned an MA in religious studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, Sarah Harding, Amelia Hall, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and L. S. Summer.

Ryan Richard Overbey studied classics, Sanskrit, and religion at Brown (-2001) and Harvard (PhD 2010). He held posts at College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. Kudo has held posts as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1933) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He lectured at Humboldt University of Berlin and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1952–1978).
Ryoichi Kondo (born 1932) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He held positions at Toyo University (~1916–1924) and Otani University (~1925–1967), and served as president of the Otani Society (~1961–1967).

Ryojun Mitomo (born 1948) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Mitomo served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor of social welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1963). Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Third Higher School and University of Tokyo, later lecturing at Ryukoku University (1897) and serving as professor at Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda (1937–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1956–1960). He held posts at Shuchiin University, Taisho University (professor ~1980–2007; emeritus ~2007–2021), and Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2014).

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Nakao held posts as a staff member at the Soto Zen Administration Research Institute and as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 1998).

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1948–1953) and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He later served as president of Taisho University (~1991–1995).

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1953–1961). Tanaka held a post at Komazawa University (~1968–2003, professor from ~1980) and served as professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami, Kouda held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Otani University (~1925–1928). He held a post at Otani University (~1949–1973) and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1973–1983).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1943–1948). Misaki later served as professor emeritus at Waseda University (attested 1988–2000).
